paragraphs: Decision center: the work of postsecondary economics teachers is to turn these front-end conditions — disciplinary training objectives and course requirements, students and classes and learning needs, economic theory and real data and literature, and assessment standards and academic integrity rules — into teachable, verifiable, and reproducible teaching and research outputs: first determine the teaching content and syllabus according to the program of study and course objectives, then prepare lecture notes and assignments and cases and datasets, then lecture and organize classroom discussion, office hours, and academic and career advising, during which assign and grade assignments and examinations and maintain grade and attendance records, then supervise student theses and internships and research, while also reading the literature, conducting economic research, and writing papers and project applications, and finally take part in department and academic committee and admissions and training work and complete handover. The point of judgment is not 'do I like teaching economics' but whether the chain of design and preparation, teaching and assessment, and research and service holds to the four things — objectives, definitions, assessment fairness, and academic integrity — and whether every step leaves a verifiable record.

Suitable for a first try: willing to explain economic theory and real data clearly and to accept repeated student questioning; able to organize content according to the syllabus and assessment standards and keep grading consistent; able to switch rhythm between lecturing, office hours, thesis supervision, and research; willing to handle student records, grades, and academic integrity matters and to consult the systems when uncertain; able to accept public speaking and long weekly hours (O*NET shows 60% of practitioners work more than 40 hours per week).

Needs caution: if you expect this job to be reading the textbook aloud or doing only research without teaching, or you are unwilling to give item-by-item explainable feedback according to the assessment standards, avoid responsibility for student data and academic integrity, treat correlation as causation and give students or the public investment or policy conclusions on that basis, or find it hard to stay patient and consistent under public lecturing and dense office hours, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: using the fictional course objectives and anonymized datasets provided on this page, complete a paper exercise that 'writes out clearly the teaching objectives, data dictionary, chart or regression interpretation, assumptions and identification limitations, and practice questions and grading rubric for one 30-minute economics micro-lesson', only to verify whether you are willing to check item by item against the objectives and definitions and to mark uncertainty truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials and does not touch real student data, and it does not constitute an investment, policy, legal, or hiring conclusion, nor is it equivalent to a teaching qualification or job training.
Decision center: whether disciplinary objectives and student needs can be turned into teaching and research outputs that students, peers, and the department can all take up and verify.

The work rhythm is determined jointly by the semester, teaching weeks, grading milestones, and research project milestones; O*NET shows 79% of practitioners have 'very large' decision freedom and 77% can determine tasks and priorities and goals themselves, but precision or accuracy is 'extremely important' for 45%, 60% work more than 40 hours per week, and public lecturing and individual office hours are interspersed.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 25-1063.00 Economics Teachers, Postsecondary. Adjacent subject teachers — agricultural sciences teachers (25-1041.00), anthropology and archeology teachers (25-1061.00), area, ethnic, and cultural studies teachers (25-1062.00), business teachers (25-1011.00), political science teachers (25-1065.00), sociology teachers (25-1067.00), and mathematical science teachers (25-1022.00) — have different disciplinary objects, methods, and outputs; postsecondary teachers are also not the same as elementary and secondary teachers or education administration or academic affairs positions. Teaching qualifications, position appointment and evaluation, and academic boundaries are governed by the regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and institutional systems, are not inferred from the job title, and must not exceed authorization to issue investment, financial planning, policy, or legal opinions externally.

AI can be treated as a controlled teaching and research aid, but generated content cannot be treated as unverified fact, a basis for grading, or a research conclusion; course objectives, assessment fairness, academic integrity determinations, and research conclusions remain the responsibility of teachers and academic institutions.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can turn economic theory and real data into teachable and testable content, whether you can give consistent and explainable feedback according to the assessment standards, whether you can keep reading the literature and conducting research, and whether you are clear about your authority boundaries on student data, academic integrity, and external advice; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of 'being good at math' or 'liking to express myself'; all of this must be confirmed in supervised teaching and teaching assistant or research experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real courses, student data, assessment and academic misconduct handling, research funding, and external consulting must be undertaken by personnel with the corresponding qualifications that follow the regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and institutional systems and academic norms; individuals must not exceed authorization to issue investment, financial planning, policy, or legal opinions externally, and this page does not constitute any investment, policy, or legal advice.

The work object of this occupation is the discipline and teaching and research context: the program of study and course objectives and syllabus, students and classes and learning needs, economic theory and real data and literature, assignments and examinations and grading standards, academic integrity and data use rules, research projects and funding and publication requirements, and the training and assessment arrangements of the department and academic committee. The output is teaching and research results that meet the course objectives and academic norms: courses completed and continuously revised according to the syllabus, verifiable lecture notes and assignments and examinations and grading records, student grades and attendance and academic records, supervised theses and internships and research, published papers and monographs and project outputs, and verifiable course evaluation and academic service records. The basis for judgment is the disciplinary method and course objectives and institutional systems, not personal habits or the job title.

Judgment one: whether course objectives and teaching content are aligned — determining teaching units and difficulty and assessment methods according to the program of study and course objectives, rather than piling up content from impression.

Judgment two: whether data and literature definitions are verified clearly — stating the data source, period, units, sample, and identification limitations, rather than treating correlation as causation.

Judgment three: whether lecturing and discussion are understandable and stay within the objectives — adjusting explanations to the students' foundation and organizing discussion, rather than only reading the notes or presenting only personal views.

Judgment four: whether assessment and grading are consistent and explainable — publishing the grading standards in advance and giving explainable feedback item by item according to the standards, rather than grading arbitrarily or changing the standards afterwards.

Judgment five: whether student records and academic integrity are held — maintaining grades and attendance and academic records as required, and handling suspected academic misconduct such as plagiarism, ghostwriting, or AI-written work according to the systems.

Judgment six: whether research and student data and external advice stay within boundaries — handling data and citations and funding and conflicts of interest per academic norms, not packaging analysis in class or public channels as investment, policy, or legal opinions beyond authorization, and not promising conclusions externally beyond authorization.

Environment and rhythm: mainly classrooms, offices, and research rooms with frequent communication with students and colleagues; email every day 96%, decision freedom 'very large' 79%, determining tasks and priorities and goals themselves 'very large' 77%, face-to-face discussions every day 51%, sitting continuously or almost continuously 47%, continuous contact with others 45%, public speaking weekly or more (not daily) 68%, indoors with controllable environment every day 80%, working more than 40 hours per week 60%, precision or accuracy 'extremely important' 45%, competition 'extremely fierce' 29%, time pressure weekly or more (not daily) 44%.

The work of postsecondary economics teachers can be divided into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is course design and preparation: determine teaching units and difficulty and assessment methods according to the program of study and course objectives, write and revise the syllabus and teaching calendar, prepare lecture notes and cases and problem sets and real datasets and reading materials, select and apply for textbooks and teaching materials, design assignments and examinations and grading standards and course evaluation methods, and adjust the starting point according to the class foundation and prerequisites. The second is teaching delivery and student learning support: lecture according to the syllabus and organize classroom discussion and group exercises, grade assignments and examinations according to the grading standards and give explainable feedback, maintain grades and attendance and academic records, hold fixed office hours to tutor students, provide academic and career course and career development guidance, and supervise undergraduate and graduate teaching, internships, and research and degree theses. The third is research, collaboration, and academic service: read the literature and exchange with colleagues and attend academic conferences to keep up with the discipline, conduct economic research and write papers and monographs and electronic information materials, write research project applications to obtain external funding, provide professional consulting to government or industry, take part in department and institutional policy and academic affairs committees as well as admissions, registration, and job placement work, and guide and assist student organizations and campus and community activities. All three work surfaces proceed within the disciplinary method, course objectives, assessment standards, and academic norms.

This occupation is responsible for teaching and assessing and supervising students according to course objectives and disciplinary methods and for the research process and citations and data and funding and conflicts of interest; the institution and academic committee and competent authorities bear management responsibility for curriculum setting, degree conferral, teacher qualifications, academic misconduct handling, and external cooperation according to regulations and systems.

Responsibilities of adjacent positions: borne by the individual teachers of each discipline and their departments and institutions according to their respective courses and academic norms, with different disciplinary bases.

In this job, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four areas: first, course objectives and assessment methods are disconnected, so the teaching content does not match the assessment requirements and students are at a loss; second, data and literature definitions are unclear or correlation is treated as causation, so explanations and conclusions are distorted; third, grading standards are inconsistent or feedback is not explainable, causing unfair assessment and appeals; fourth, student records and academic integrity and conflicts of interest are handled improperly, or classroom analysis is packaged beyond authorization as investment or policy opinions, causing academic and compliance risk. The verification method is that each item has a basis that can be looked back on: the syllabus and teaching calendar and grading standards, lecture notes and data dictionary and literature and identification limitation notes, grading and feedback and grade and attendance records, and academic integrity and data use and conflict of interest and project and funding records, rather than memory or verbal understanding.

Record grades and attendance and academic and research data and citations according to the course objectives and academic norms and complete handover; records should agree with the grading standards and course evaluation to facilitate verification; suspected academic misconduct and conflicts of interest are handled per the systems with records kept.

Ministry of Education Order No. 40 applies to scientific research and related activities at higher education institutions: the school is the prevention and handling body, and the academic committee investigates/determines according to law; teachers guide students on academic norms and review theses when necessary, and a personal or AI plagiarism check score cannot be used for direct determination. Reports are handled by the designated receiving department, and personnel who contact the materials keep confidentiality; investigation, defense, determination, handling, and review follow the procedures. The specific rules for course grading/examination cheating are verified separately, and the research measures cannot be generalized to all grade disputes. Data breach response follows the actual legal obligations/institutional procedures, and registration before reporting cannot be set as a uniform sequence.

Common collaborators: students and teaching assistants, colleagues in the same and other departments, academic affairs and research management and student affairs offices, the library and teaching technology departments, and the academic committee and journals and project reviewers.

Common tools and objects: learning management systems (LMS) and teaching platforms, textbooks and lecture notes and cases and public datasets and statistical and econometric software, literature and databases and citation and reproduction tools, assignment and examination and grading and academic integrity detection tools, grade and attendance and student information systems, and office and presentation and online meeting tools.

Research academic misconduct follows the school/academic committee procedures and is not determined by a teacher or AI on their own; the specific course grading appeal system was not obtained.

paragraphs: Agricultural sciences teachers (25-1041.00)
Teach agricultural systems and agronomy courses and conduct agronomic research, responsible for teaching crop and soil and agricultural economics and agricultural technology content clearly.

The disciplinary object and basis differ: agricultural sciences teachers focus on agricultural systems and biology and soil and agricultural technology under agronomy and related standards; this page's occupation focuses on economic theory and real data and econometric methods under economics methods and course objectives. Both are postsecondary subject teaching positions, but the disciplinary object and method and course basis differ and cannot be interchanged by school name.

If you want to teach agronomy and agricultural systems and conduct agronomic research, you can choose the agricultural sciences teacher direction; if you want to teach economic theory and data and econometric methods, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Anthropology and archeology teachers (25-1061.00)
Teach anthropology and archeology courses and conduct research on culture and remains, responsible for teaching field evidence and cultural interpretation clearly.

The disciplinary object and method differ: anthropology and archeology teachers focus on culture and remains and field methods under archaeology and cultural studies norms; this page's occupation focuses on economic theory and statistical data and econometric identification strategies, with different evidence types and methods. Both are postsecondary subject teaching positions, but the methods cannot be interchanged.

If you want to teach culture and remains and conduct field research, you can choose the anthropology and archeology teacher direction; if you want to teach economic theory and data analysis, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Area, ethnic, and cultural studies teachers (25-1062.00)

The disciplinary object differs: area, ethnic, and cultural studies teachers focus on regions and ethnic groups and cultural comparison under area studies methods; this page's occupation focuses on economic theory and data and econometric methods, with different units of analysis and evidence types.

If you want to do regional and ethnic and cultural comparison research, you can choose that direction; if you want to teach economics courses and data analysis, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Business teachers (25-1011.00)

The course positioning differs: business teachers lean toward management, operations, and applied business courses and cases and enterprise practice; this page's occupation leans toward economic theory and empirical methods, with economic phenomena and data as the object of analysis rather than enterprise operations practice. The courses and assessment standards differ.

If you want to teach management and operations and applied business courses, you can choose the business teacher direction; if you want to teach microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics courses, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Political science teachers (25-1065.00)

The disciplinary object differs: political science teachers focus on political institutions and power and public decision-making; this page's occupation focuses on economic theory and markets and incentives and econometric methods. Although the two are adjacent (for example, where public economics and political economy overlap), the course basis and research methods differ.

If you want to teach political institutions and public decision-making, you can choose the political science teacher direction; if you want to teach economic theory and empirical methods, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Sociology teachers (25-1067.00)

The disciplinary object differs: sociology teachers focus on social structure and social relations and social survey methods; this page's occupation focuses on economic theory and statistical data and econometric methods, with different theoretical frameworks and evidence types, and cannot be interchanged within the broad social sciences category.

If you want to teach social structure and social survey methods, you can choose the sociology teacher direction; if you want to teach economic theory and econometric analysis, this page's occupation is more suitable.

Observation signal one: willing to explain economic theory and real data clearly and to accept repeated student questioning, and able to work according to course objectives and assessment standards rather than by feel.

Observation signal two: willing to follow academic integrity and data use and copyright and privacy rules, and to confirm before acting where grading and academic misconduct and external advice are involved.

Observation signal three: able to stay careful about definitions and grading under dense lecturing and office hours and grading and thesis supervision, and not to skip verification to keep up the pace.

Observation signal four: able to accept a rhythm driven by the semester and teaching weeks and examinations and grading and research projects, and willing to do student records and academic service and continuous learning.

Trainable abilities include course and syllabus design, preparation of lecture notes and cases and problem sets and datasets, classroom lecturing and discussion organization, assignment and examination grading and feedback, academic and career advising, thesis and internship and research supervision, literature retrieval and academic writing, data analysis and econometric methods, and academic integrity and data use and records.

entries.answer: Write and revise the syllabus and teaching calendar according to the program of study and course objectives and prepare lecture notes and cases and problem sets and datasets and reading materials and select textbooks; lecture and organize classroom discussion and group exercises according to the syllabus and adjust to the students' foundation; grade assignments and examinations according to the grading standards and give explainable feedback and maintain grade and attendance and academic records; hold fixed office hours and academic and career advising and supervise theses and internships and research; read the literature and attend academic conferences and conduct economic research and write papers and monographs and apply for projects; take part in department and academic committee and admissions and training work and guide new teachers and student organizations and campus and community activities.
entries.question: What does a postsecondary economics teacher do on a typical day?

entries.answer: This page's occupation teaches microeconomics and macroeconomics and econometrics and price theory with economic theory and real data and econometric methods and conducts economics research; agricultural sciences teachers focus on agricultural systems, anthropology and archeology teachers focus on culture and remains, area, ethnic, and cultural studies teachers focus on regional and ethnic and cultural comparison, and business teachers lean toward management, operations, and applied business courses. Postsecondary teachers are also not the same as elementary and secondary teachers or education administration and academic affairs positions. description.text: Postsecondary economics teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-1063.00) teach microeconomics and macroeconomics and econometrics and price theory and other courses in higher education and conduct economics research: they design the syllabus and lecture notes and cases and datasets according to the program of study and course objectives, lecture and organize discussion according to the syllabus, grade assignments and examinations according to the standards and maintain grade and attendance and academic records, hold fixed office hours and academic and career advising, supervise theses and internships and research, read the literature and conduct economic research and write papers and project applications, and take part in department and academic committee work. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 123,920 USD per year (only the median is provided); 2024 employment was about 15,800, and the 2024—2034 projection is 'slower than average (1% to 2%)' with about 1,200 projected openings; the preparation level is Job Zone Five and the interest code is SI. subject.name: Postsecondary economics teachers
subject.summary: Postsecondary economics teachers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 25-1063.00, Economics Teachers, Postsecondary) are teaching and research positions in higher education disciplines: postsecondary teachers who teach economics courses covering microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, and price theory, including teaching-focused positions and positions with both teaching and research; the work includes writing and revising the syllabus and teaching calendar according to the program of study and course objectives, preparing lecture notes and cases and problem sets and real datasets and reading materials, selecting textbooks and teaching materials, lecturing and organizing classroom discussion and group exercises according to the syllabus, grading assignments and examinations according to the grading standards and giving explainable feedback, maintaining grades and attendance and academic records, holding fixed office hours and academic and career advising, supervising theses and internships and research, reading the literature and attending academic conferences, conducting economic research and writing papers and monographs, writing project applications to obtain funding, providing professional consulting to government or industry, and taking part in department and academic committee and admissions and training work and guiding student organizations and campus and community activities. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 123,920 USD per year (that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles or an hourly figure); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 15,800, a 2024—2034 projection of 'slower than average (Slower than average, 1% to 2%)', and about 1,200 projected job openings (that page uses a projection period total definition); the preparation level is Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 or higher), the education feedback is 81% doctoral degree and 10% post-master's certificate and 7% master's degree, the interest code is SI, and there are 22 tasks; the work context includes email every day 96%, decision freedom 'very large' 79%, determining tasks and priorities and goals themselves 'very large' 77%, face-to-face discussions every day 51%, sitting continuously or almost continuously 47%, public speaking weekly or more (not daily) 68%, indoors with controllable environment every day 80%, working more than 40 hours per week 60%, precision or accuracy 'extremely important' 45%, competition 'extremely fierce' 29%, and time pressure weekly or more (not daily) 44%. Mainland China definition: postsecondary teachers should obtain a higher education institution teacher qualification under the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China and the Teacher Qualification Regulations (State Council Order No. 188) and teach within the scope of recognition, and positions are mostly filled through open recruitment by public institutions and institutional evaluation and appointment. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage definition corresponding to this occupation, this page preserves the gap as it stands, and industry average wages serve only as a visible industry proxy.
